variations: Healing isn't patching the hole. It's you growing big enough that the hole becomes part of you.
You don't have to forget them to live well. Living well means taking them with you.

items.sourceNote: Robert Louis Stevenson「dogs in heaven first」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 有人問我，天堂會不會有狗？我說，牠們早就在了，而且比我們任何一個人都先到，正搖著尾巴，在門口幫我們佔好位子等著呢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 帶點微笑的告別語，適合宗教信仰較淡但相信「牠在某個好地方等我」的飼主
variations: 如果天堂沒有毛孩，那我寧願去牠們在的那個地方。
牠不是離開了，是先去把最好的位子搶下來，留給以後的我。

en.content: Someone asked me if there are dogs in heaven. I said they got there long before any of us — tails already wagging, saving us the best spot right by the gate.
en.editorNote: A goodbye with a small smile in it; good for owners who aren't especially religious but like the idea that 'they're somewhere good, waiting'
variations: If heaven doesn't have room for the furry ones, then I'd rather go wherever they went.
They didn't leave. They just went ahead to grab the best seat and hold it for me.

items.sourceNote: 「pawprint left on my heart」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你不在我身邊了，可是你走過的地方，全都留著小小的腳印——包括我的心。那幾個印子擦不掉，我也不想擦掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合刻在紀念品、腳印黏土模上的題字，或紀念貼文的短句
variations: 家裡到處都被你踩過。最深的那個，踩在我心上。
你走了以後我才發現，你把腳印留在了我這輩子都到得了的地方。

en.content: You're not by my side anymore, but everywhere you walked, you left tiny pawprints — including one right across my heart. That one won't wash off, and I don't want it to.
en.editorNote: Good as an inscription on a keepsake or clay pawprint mold, or a short caption for a memorial post
variations: You tracked prints all over this house. The deepest one landed on my heart.
After you left, I realized you pressed a pawprint somewhere I'll always be able to reach it.

items.sourceNote: 英女王「grief is the price we pay for love」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你現在有多痛，就代表你們當初有多愛。悲傷是我們為愛付的帳單，不是你哪裡做錯了。願意心碎，本身就是一種很勇敢的溫柔。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給正在自責、覺得「我是不是太脆弱了」的飼主，把悲傷正常化為愛的證明
variations: 會這麼捨不得，是因為牠真的被你好好愛過。這不是弱，這是你付出過的證據。
眼淚不用不好意思。那是愛滿出來，找不到地方放而已。

en.content: How much it hurts now is just a measure of how much you loved. Grief is the bill we pay for love — it doesn't mean you did anything wrong. Being willing to break like this is its own kind of brave.
en.editorNote: For an owner spiraling into self-blame or wondering if they're 'too fragile'; normalizes grief as proof of love
variations: It hurts to let go this much because they were truly, well loved. That's not weakness — it's the receipt for everything you gave.
Don't apologize for the tears. That's just love overflowing with nowhere to go.

items.sourceNote: 空碗／項圈掛勾／沙發固定位 的日常物件觸發悲傷，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 最想你的時候，往往不是大日子，是那個不用再裝飼料的碗、那條還掛在門邊的牽繩、沙發上那塊你窩了好多年、現在空空的位子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合離世後一兩週、開始被日常小物件狙擊的飼主；把「突然崩潰」正常化
variations: 傷心不挑時間。它躲在還沒收的碗、還掛著的牽繩、和你那塊坐得凹下去的沙發角。
原來想念不是轟轟烈烈的，是走過那個空碗時，腳步慢了半拍。

en.content: The moments I miss you most aren't the big ones. It's the bowl I don't have to fill anymore, the leash still hanging by the door, and your spot on the couch that suddenly looks way too empty.
en.editorNote: For an owner a week or two out, getting ambushed by ordinary objects; normalizes sudden waves of grief
variations: Grief doesn't wait for the anniversary. It hides in the unfilled bowl, the hook by the door, and the dented cushion where you used to curl up.
Turns out missing you isn't loud. It's just my footsteps slowing down as I pass your empty bowl.

items.sourceNote: 遺物盒／memory box 儀式（項圈、玩具、腳印收好）frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 把你的項圈、那顆咬到脫線的玩具、還有你的小腳印，一起收進盒子裡。不是要把你收起來忘掉，是先幫這些回憶找個家，等我哪天夠勇敢了，再慢慢一件一件拿出來想你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給不知道該怎麼處理遺物、又捨不得丟的飼主，提供一個溫柔的「先收好」做法
variations: 遺物不用急著丟，也不用逼自己天天看。找個盒子好好裝著，想你的時候再打開就好。
把牠的東西收進盒子的那天，我沒有在告別，我只是把愛先好好保存起來。

en.content: I put your collar, that toy you chewed to threads, and your little paw print all in one box. Not to pack you away and forget — just to give these memories a home, and open it piece by piece on the days I'm brave enough to miss you.
en.editorNote: For an owner who can't bear to toss their pet's things but doesn't know what to do with them; offers a gentle 'keep it safe for now' ritual
variations: You don't have to throw their things out, and you don't have to stare at them daily. Just tuck them in a box and open it when the missing comes.
The day I boxed up your things, I wasn't saying goodbye. I was just keeping the love somewhere safe.

items.sourceNote: 寫信給毛孩＋他日重逢（until we meet again）frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 親愛的，我今天又忍不住喊了你的名字。沒關係，你不用回頭。我只是想讓你知道，這裡一切都好，你被想念得很用力。等我這輩子走完，換我去找你，我們再一起散一次好長好長的步。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合做成寫給毛孩的一封信、告別式念稿，或忌日當天的紀念貼文
variations: 如果那邊有草地，先幫我們佔一塊好位子。我會晚一點到，但一定會到。
先去玩吧，別等我。等時候到了，我認得出你的叫聲，你也一定認得出我。

en.content: Hey buddy — I called your name again today. It's okay, you don't have to turn around. I just wanted you to know everything's alright here, and you are missed so, so hard. When my own walk is done, I'll come find you, and we'll take one more long, long stroll together.
en.editorNote: Works as a letter to your pet, a reading at a memorial, or a post on the anniversary of their passing
variations: If there's a field over there, save us a good spot. I'll be late, but I'll be there.
Go play — don't wait up for me. When the time comes, I'll know your bark, and you'll know me too.

items.sourceNote: 「愛得深所以捨不得」frame（How lucky I am…），原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 會這麼捨不得，是因為我們真的很愛很愛。這份痛，其實是愛還在的證明——你沒有白疼牠一場。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回覆自責「是不是太脆弱」的飼主，把眼淚重新定義成愛的證據
variations: 如果分開不痛，那才代表沒認真愛過。你會這麼難過，是因為你們之間是真的。
眼淚不是你不夠堅強，是牠在你生命裡佔的位置，真的很大很大。

en.content: It hurts this much because you loved this much. The ache isn't weakness — it's proof the love is still here, and that they were never loved for nothing.
en.editorNote: For the owner blaming themselves for 'falling apart'; reframes the tears as evidence of love
variations: If goodbye didn't hurt, it would mean it was never real. You're hurting because the two of you were the real thing.
The tears aren't you being fragile. They're the size of the space they filled in your life.

items.sourceNote: 「換了一個房間 / different rooms」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 牠沒有離開，只是走到了我看不見的那個房間。牆很薄，愛還在流通，只是我暫時沒辦法推開那扇門。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合安慰覺得「牠完全消失了」的飼主，也適合放進紀念卡片內頁
variations: 我們不是失去了牠，只是暫時待在不同的房間。等我這邊的燈熄了，我就過去找牠。
看不見不等於不在。牠只是先進了另一個房間，把門為我留了一條縫。

en.content: They didn't leave — they just walked into a room I can't see. The wall is thin, the love still passes through it, I just can't push that door open yet.
en.editorNote: For an owner who feels their pet is 'completely gone'; also works inside a memorial card
variations: We didn't lose them. We're just in different rooms for now. When my lights go out, I'll go find them.
Out of sight isn't gone. They stepped into the next room and left the door open a crack for me.

items.sourceNote: 「腳印留在心上 / paw prints on my heart」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你的腳掌不再踩在地板上了，卻整整齊齊踩進了我心裡。以後每一步我往前走，都帶著你留下的印子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合刻在紀念項鍊、木牌，或做成忌日的紀念貼文
variations: 地上的腳印會被雨沖掉，心上那排不會。你會一直陪我走下去，用你的方式。
你把小小的腳印留在我心上當路標，以後我不會走丟——因為有你在前面帶路。

en.content: Your paws don't tap across the floor anymore, but they pressed a neat little trail right into my heart. Every step I take from here carries the prints you left.
en.editorNote: Good engraved on a keepsake necklace or wooden plaque, or as an anniversary post
variations: The prints on the ground wash away in the rain. The ones on my heart don't. You'll keep walking with me, your way.
You left your little paw prints on my heart as trail markers, so I'll never get lost — you're up ahead, leading the way.

items.sourceNote: 「把愛傳下去 / 用牠的名字做好事」療癒行動 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 如果太想牠了，就用牠的名字去對別的生命好一點吧。捐一包飼料、摸一隻流浪貓、多抱身邊的孩子一下——牠給你的溫柔，還可以繼續傳下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給走到「想為牠做點什麼」階段的飼主，把思念轉成具體、能執行的行動
variations: 想牠的時候，就替牠去愛一下這個世界。牠教會你的溫柔，不用跟著牠一起被埋起來。
牠沒辦法再回來，但牠留在你身上的善良可以出門。用牠的名字，去接住下一個需要的小生命。

en.content: When you miss them too much, be a little kinder to some other living thing in their name. Donate a bag of food, pet a stray, hug the kid next to you a beat longer — the gentleness they gave you can keep going.
en.editorNote: For the owner ready to 'do something for them'; turns grief into a concrete, doable action
variations: When you miss them, go love the world a little on their behalf. The tenderness they taught you doesn't have to be buried with them.
They can't come back, but the kindness they left in you can head out the door. In their name, catch the next small life that needs it.

items.sourceNote: 「臨終不說『不要走』，好好放手」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 牠走的那一刻，你沒有哭著求牠留下，而是輕輕說「可以了，去吧，我沒事」。那不是不愛，那是你能給牠最溫柔、最勇敢的一次愛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些後悔「當時是不是該多留牠一下」的飼主，肯定放手也是一種深愛
variations: 你忍著不喊「不要走」，是怕牠捨不得你、走得辛苦。這份體貼，牠一定收到了。
放手很痛，但你替牠選了不再痛。這是最難的溫柔，你做到了。

en.content: In their last moment, you didn't cry and beg them to stay — you whispered, 'It's okay, you can go, I'll be alright.' That wasn't loving them less. That was the gentlest, bravest love you had left to give.
en.editorNote: For owners who regret 'not holding on a little longer'; affirms that letting go is also deep love
variations: You swallowed the 'please don't go' so they wouldn't leave feeling torn about you. They felt that kindness — I promise.
Letting go hurt, but you chose no-more-hurting for them. That's the hardest tenderness there is, and you did it.

items.sourceNote: 「grief is like the ocean, waves」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 想牠這件事，像海浪。有時候一整天都很平靜，有時候一個罐頭的味道就把你整個人淹過去。不用逼自己站穩，浪來了就讓它來，退了你還在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給喪寵一段時間、以為自己好了卻突然崩潰的人，告訴他情緒起伏是正常的
variations: 難過不會照著日曆走。今天笑得出來，不代表明天不能哭，這都算數。
你不是退步了，你只是又想牠了。浪一波波來，這很正常。

en.content: Missing them comes in waves. Some days the water's calm all day, then the smell of one can of food pulls you right under. You don't have to stay standing — let the wave come, and when it goes, you're still here.
en.editorNote: For someone who thought they'd healed and then suddenly fell apart; normalizes the ups and downs
variations: Grief doesn't follow a calendar. Laughing today doesn't mean you can't cry tomorrow — both count.
You didn't go backwards. You just missed them again. The waves keep coming, and that's normal.

items.sourceNote: 「空掉的日常、無聲的門口」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 最難的不是那天，是之後。是開門沒有人衝出來，是半夜沒有腳步聲，是碗還放在原位、你卻沒東西可以裝。原來一隻毛孩，撐起的是一整套日常。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給離世一陣子、被生活裡各種「空掉的小習慣」反覆刺到的飼主
variations: 你以為會哭在牠走的那天，結果哭在洗到牠碗的那一刻。
回家鑰匙轉開的那一秒，還是會等一下——等那個再也不會來的迎接。

en.content: The hardest part isn't that day — it's after. The door opening with no one rushing to it. No little footsteps at 2am. The bowl still in its spot, and nothing left to fill it with. Turns out one small animal was holding up your whole routine.
en.editorNote: For owners who keep getting caught off guard by the small empty habits weeks after the loss
variations: You thought you'd cry on the day they left. You cried while washing their bowl instead.
The key still turns in the lock and you still pause — waiting for a welcome that isn't coming.

items.sourceNote: 「寫信給毛孩、看照片、繼續對話」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 如果還是很想牠，就繼續跟牠說話吧。回家喊一聲、睡前道晚安、遇到好事跟牠報備。愛沒有因為牠走了就斷線，只是換一種方式繼續。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給覺得「一直想牠是不是不正常」的飼主，肯定持續的思念也是一種健康的陪伴
variations: 翻照片不是折磨自己，是提醒自己——你們真的一起快樂過那麼多天。
你可以寫封信給牠，把來不及說的都寫下來。牠讀得到的方式，跟我們不一樣而已。

en.content: If you still miss them, keep talking to them. Call out when you get home, say goodnight before bed, tell them when something good happens. The love didn't get cut off when they left — it just found a new way to keep going.
en.editorNote: For owners who wonder if 'still thinking about them all the time' is unhealthy; affirms ongoing remembrance
variations: Looking through the photos isn't torturing yourself. It's proof you really were happy together, all those days.
Write them a letter with everything you didn't get to say. They read it a different way than we do — but they read it.

items.sourceNote: 「你會痊癒，但不會再是原來的你」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 有一天你會好起來，這是真的。但你不會變回失去牠之前的你——你會帶著牠一起，重新長成一個更懂得愛、也更捨得放手的人。牠沒有離開，牠住進你怎麼看世界的方式裡了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給走過最痛階段、正在慢慢復原的飼主，肯定改變不是遺忘
variations: 痊癒不是把牠忘掉，是學會帶著這份想念，還能好好過日子。
你身上有一塊，是牠留下來的。那塊會一直在，這樣很好。

en.content: One day you'll be okay again — that part's true. But you won't go back to who you were before you lost them. You'll grow around it, into someone who loves a little deeper and knows how to let go. They didn't leave. They moved into the way you see the world.
en.editorNote: For owners past the worst of it and slowly healing; affirms that being changed isn't forgetting
variations: Healing isn't forgetting them. It's learning to carry the missing and still live well.
There's a part of you now that they left behind. That part stays for good — and that's a good thing.

items.sourceNote: 獸醫「慶幸是他先離開」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 還好是你先走的。生老病死這種事，我懂，你不懂。如果換成是你留下來，你會每天在門口等一個不會回來的人，搞不懂我為什麼消失，那種想念沒人幫你解釋。所以這些難過就讓我來扛吧，你什麼都不用煩惱，這樣才對。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給陷入「當初該多做點什麼」自責的飼主，把痛苦留給自己承擔反而是一種釋懷
variations: 你不用懂什麼叫離別，這件事交給我就好。你只要記得，你被愛過，滿滿的那種。
幸好等待的人是我不是你。我知道你去了哪裡，你不用困惑，這樣我就放心了。

en.content: I'm glad you went first. You never understood sickness and goodbyes — I do. If I'd left you behind, you'd wait at the door every day for someone who wasn't coming back, never understanding why I vanished, with no one to explain it. So let me be the one to carry all of this. You don't have to worry about a thing. That's how it should be.
en.editorNote: For owners stuck on 'I should have done more'; reframes bearing the pain alone as a kind of peace
variations: You never had to learn what goodbye means. Leave that part to me. Just remember you were loved — the whole, overflowing kind.
Thank goodness the one left waiting is me and not you. I know where you went. You don't have to be confused, and that lets me rest.

items.sourceNote: 「Grief is just love with nowhere to go」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你以為那是悲傷，其實那是愛。只是那份愛突然沒地方去了，就堆在心裡，脹得發疼。別急著把它清掉——它會慢慢學會，換一種方式待在你身邊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給覺得自己「怎麼還走不出來」而焦慮的飼主，肯定思念本身就是愛的證明
variations: 你哭得那麼慘，不是因為軟弱，是因為愛得很深。這兩件事一直都是同一件事。
想念沒有停下來的一天，因為愛也沒有。它只是換了個地方，繼續住著。

en.content: You think it's grief, but it's really love — love that suddenly has nowhere to go, so it piles up inside you until it aches. Don't rush to clear it out. Little by little, it learns a new way to stay close.
en.editorNote: For owners anxious that they 'still haven't moved on'; affirms that missing them is proof of the love
variations: You're not falling apart because you're weak. You're falling apart because you loved that deep. It was always the same thing.
The missing never fully stops, because the love never did. It just found somewhere new to live.

items.sourceNote: 「Dogs find the people who need them」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 牠不是剛好走進你的生命，是牠一路找過來的。牠嗅到你心裡有個空洞，你自己都還沒發現，牠就先來把那裡填滿了。這種相遇，這輩子不會有第二次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合紀念文、告別式追思詞，或飼主寫給自己回顧這段緣分的話
variations: 牠選中你，不是意外。是你需要牠的那一刻，牠就已經在往你這邊走了。
有些空缺，你要等到被填滿了，才知道它一直都在。謝謝牠讓你發現這件事。

en.content: They didn't just wander into your life — they came looking. They caught the shape of an empty place inside you, one you hadn't even noticed yet, and filled it before you knew it was there. A meeting like that doesn't happen twice.
en.editorNote: Good for a memorial tribute, eulogy, or an owner looking back on how they met
variations: They choosing you was no accident. The moment you needed them, they were already headed your way.
Some empty spaces you only notice once they've been filled. Thank them for showing you it was there.

items.sourceNote: 獸醫「用開放式問句陪伴，別急著給答案」frame，原創改寫（安慰他人角度）

zh-tw.content: 朋友的毛孩走了，別急著說「牠去更好的地方了」「再養一隻就好」。你只要輕輕問一句：「你有沒有什麼話還想跟牠說？」然後安靜地聽。有時候最溫柔的安慰，是不給答案，只給時間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給想安慰喪寵朋友、卻怕說錯話的人，實用的陪伴指引
variations: 不用想漂亮的句子。一句「我在，你想哭就哭」，比一百句道理都有用。
別幫他決定該多久走出來。你只要說：不急，我陪你慢慢來。

en.content: When a friend's pet dies, don't rush to say 'they're in a better place' or 'you can always get another one.' Just ask, softly, 'Is there anything you still wish you could tell them?' — and then listen. Sometimes the gentlest comfort isn't an answer. It's time.
en.editorNote: For someone who wants to comfort a grieving friend but is afraid of saying the wrong thing
variations: You don't need the perfect words. 'I'm here, cry if you need to' beats a hundred wise sayings.
Don't decide for them how long healing should take. Just say: no rush, I'll go at your pace.

items.sourceNote: 「Until one has loved an animal, a part of one's soul remains unawakened」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 在遇見牠之前，你心裡有一塊地方是沉睡的。是牠把那裡叫醒的——教你怎麼毫無保留地愛一個生命，也教你怎麼在牠走後，還帶著這份溫柔活下去。那塊醒過來的地方，永遠不會再睡回去了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給走過喪寵、想肯定這段陪伴帶來改變的飼主，語氣溫暖而不悲
variations: 牠喚醒了你身上最柔軟的那一塊，那份柔軟不會隨牠離開，會一直留在你身上。
愛過牠之後，你變成一個更會愛的人。這是牠留給你最後也最好的禮物。

en.content: Before you met them, there was a part of your heart still asleep. They're the one who woke it — taught you how to love a life with nothing held back, and how to keep carrying that tenderness even after they're gone. That awakened part of you never falls back asleep.
en.editorNote: For owners past the loss who want to honor how the bond changed them; warm rather than sorrowful
variations: They woke the softest part of you, and that softness doesn't leave when they do. It stays.
After loving them, you became someone better at loving. That's the last and finest gift they left you.

items.sourceNote: 「you gave them a good life」guilt-relief frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你一直在問自己「我是不是還能為牠多做點什麼」。可是換個角度看：牠這一生從來不用擔心下一餐在哪、不用怕冷、不用怕沒人要——因為牠的整個世界，就是你。你給的不是「一隻寵物該有的」，是一輩子被好好愛著的日子。這件事，走了也帶不走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給反覆自責「有沒有做得不夠」的飼主，把焦點從遺憾拉回「你已經給了牠一整個安穩的人生」
variations: 牠或許只活了幾年，但那幾年牠是被捧在手心的。有些人活一輩子都沒被這樣愛過，牠有——因為有你。
別再算「還能不能多做一點」了。你早就把最重要的那件事做完了：讓牠這輩子，天天都知道自己有家。

en.content: You keep asking yourself, 'Could I have done more?' But look at it another way: their whole life, they never once had to worry where the next meal was, never had to be cold, never had to fear being unwanted — because their entire world was you. What you gave them wasn't the bare minimum. It was a lifetime of being deeply loved. That's something death can't take back.
en.editorNote: For owners stuck on 'did I do enough' — pulls the focus off regret and onto the whole safe life they already gave
variations: Maybe they only got a few years. But every one of them, they were held like something precious. Some beings live a whole life without that. Yours had it — because of you.
Stop tallying what more you could've done. You already did the one thing that mattered: you made sure they knew, every single day, that they had a home.

items.sourceNote: 託夢／夢中相見 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 如果哪天你在夢裡看見我——別急著醒。那不是你想太多，是我趁你睡著了，偷偷跑回來看看你有沒有好好吃飯、有沒有記得笑。看一眼我就走，不吵你。你只要在夢裡多抱我一下下就好，其他的，等我們下次見。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寵物離世後常夢見毛孩、或渴望再見一面的飼主，語氣溫柔帶點俏皮
variations: 夢見我不用怕，那是我來報平安。彩虹橋這邊很好，你別擔心，記得替我也好好過。
睡不著的時候就想著我。說不定一閉上眼，我就從門口小跑步過來了。

en.content: If one night you see me in a dream — don't rush to wake up. You're not imagining it. I snuck back while you were sleeping, just to check you're eating right and still remembering how to smile. One look and I'll go, I won't keep you. Just hold me a little longer in the dream. Everything else can wait till next time.
en.editorNote: For owners who dream of their pet, or long for one more glimpse; tender with a light, playful touch
variations: Don't be scared when you dream of me — that's just me stopping by to say I'm okay. It's nice over here on the bridge. Live well for me too.
When you can't sleep, think of me. Close your eyes and maybe I'll come trotting up from the doorway like I always did.

items.sourceNote: 「最想念的一件事」日常聲音消失 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 沒有人告訴我，最難熬的不是大哭那幾天，是家裡忽然變得好安靜。以前你指甲踏在地板上的聲音、翻身的聲音、聽到我回家衝過來的聲音——現在全沒了。這個家還是這個家，只是少了那些屬於你的雜音，安靜得讓人心慌。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫「家裡突然安靜下來」這個常被忽略卻最痛的思念點，適合離世一段時間後仍不適應的飼主
variations: 我不是想哭才難過，是我泡咖啡的時候，習慣性等你跑過來討摸，卻等不到那個聲音了。
原來想念一個生命，是想念牠製造的所有聲音。那些以前嫌吵的，現在全變成我最想再聽一次的。

en.content: Nobody warned me the hardest part wouldn't be the days of crying. It's how quiet the house suddenly got. The click of your nails on the floor, the sound of you rolling over, the scramble when you heard me come home — all gone now. It's the same house. It's just missing every little noise that was yours, and the silence sets my heart on edge.
en.editorNote: Captures the overlooked ache of a suddenly silent house; for owners still not used to it a while after the loss
variations: It's not that I want to cry. It's that I pour my coffee and still wait for you to come running for a scratch — and the sound never comes.
Turns out missing someone is missing every noise they made. All the racket I used to sigh at is exactly what I'd give anything to hear once more.

items.sourceNote: 「changed form, not gone」自然萬物寄託 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 牠沒有消失，只是換了個樣子陪你。以前牠只待在沙發那個角落、門口那塊地墊上；現在牠在早上灑進窗戶的那道陽光裡、在吹過陽台的風裡、在你突然想笑的那一秒裡。你以為失去了牠，其實牠從一個位置，散進了你整天的每個縫隙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把「牠不見了」reframe 成「牠變成無所不在」，適合喜歡自然寄託、想在日常中感覺毛孩還在的飼主
variations: 牠不再只在某個角落等你，牠變成風、變成光、變成你路過公園時心頭那陣暖。想牠的時候，抬頭看看，牠其實到處都在。
從前牠在你身邊一個小小的位置，現在牠在你身邊的每一個地方。這不是失去，是牠終於能無所不在地陪著你。

en.content: They didn't disappear. They just changed shape to stay with you. They used to live in that one corner of the couch, that one mat by the door. Now they're in the light that spills through the window each morning, in the breeze crossing the balcony, in the split second something makes you smile. You thought you lost them. Really, they went from one spot to every gap in your whole day.
en.editorNote: Reframes 'they're gone' into 'they're everywhere'; for owners drawn to finding their pet in nature and daily life
variations: They don't wait in one corner anymore. They became the wind, the light, the warmth in your chest when you pass the park. When you miss them, just look up — they're everywhere.
They used to take up one small place beside you. Now they're in every place beside you. That's not losing them. That's them finally able to be everywhere at once.

items.sourceNote: 「thank you for the ordinary days」日常感謝 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 我沒辦法謝你什麼豐功偉業，因為我們一起做的，全是最普通的小事：一起賴床、一起等外送、一起看窗外發呆。可是回頭看才懂，就是那幾千個平凡到不行的早晨，把我這輩子撐成了現在最想念的樣子。謝謝你把那麼多再普通不過的日子，變成我捨不得的日子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 感謝 register，但聚焦「日常小事」而非戲劇性時刻，適合紀念文或回顧陪伴歲月的飼主
variations: 我們沒去過什麼遠方，就在這個小小的家，一天過一天。但那些一天，現在每一天我都好想重來一次。
最想謝你的，不是哪件大事，是你每天在門口等我回家的那個畫面。原來幸福，一直都藏在那麼小的地方。

en.content: I can't thank you for anything grand, because everything we did together was the plainest small stuff: sleeping in, waiting on the delivery, staring out the window at nothing. But looking back, I finally get it — it was those few thousand utterly ordinary mornings that quietly built my life into the thing I now miss most. Thank you for turning so many nothing-special days into days I can't bear to give up.
en.editorNote: Gratitude register, but focused on ordinary daily life rather than dramatic moments; for memorial notes or looking back on the years together
variations: We never went anywhere far. We just lived, one day at a time, in our little home. But every one of those days, I'd give anything to have back now.
What I most want to thank you for isn't some big thing. It's the sight of you waiting at the door for me to come home. Turns out happiness was hiding in something that small the whole time.

items.sourceNote: 「你已經盡力了、牠從沒怪過你」化解自責 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你一直在算那些「早知道」：早知道那天就帶去看醫生、早知道就不出門那麼久。可是你有沒有想過，牠從來沒有一秒在心裡怪過你。在牠的世界裡，你不是那個做錯的人，你是每天回家會蹲下來抱牠的那個人。你以為你欠牠一句對不起，其實牠只想聽你說一句：我知道你已經盡力了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 專門接住陷在自責裡的飼主，把焦點從「我哪裡做錯」轉回「毛孩眼中的你」，適合私訊給正在崩潰的朋友
variations: 牠不會用那些「早知道」來記得你。牠記得的，是你的味道、你的手、還有每次你開門那一秒牠有多開心。放過自己，也是牠會想要的。
你把自己判了刑，可是牠早就替你無罪釋放了。牠只認得那個愛牠的你，從來沒認得那個你以為做錯的你。

en.content: You keep running the 'if only' list: if only I'd taken them to the vet that day, if only I hadn't been out so long. But here's the thing — they never blamed you, not for one second. In their world you weren't the one who got it wrong. You were the one who crouched down to hug them every time you got home. You think you owe them an apology. All they ever wanted to hear was: I know you did everything you could.
en.editorNote: Built to catch owners stuck in self-blame; shifts the focus from 'what I did wrong' back to 'who I was in their eyes' — good to send a friend who's falling apart
variations: They won't remember you by your 'if onlys.' They remember your smell, your hands, and how happy they were the second you opened the door. Letting yourself off the hook is what they'd want too.
You sentenced yourself. They acquitted you a long time ago. They only ever knew the you who loved them — never the you who thinks they got it wrong.

items.sourceNote: 「悲傷是愛的代價」reframe frame，原創改寫（Queen Elizabeth 名句意象改寫）

zh-tw.content: 會這麼痛，是因為你真的很愛牠。這種痛沒有捷徑、沒有速成，因為它其實就是愛，只是換了一個現在很難承受的樣子。所以不用急著「好起來」，也不用假裝沒事。你現在流的每一滴眼淚，都是在替那幾年的愛結帳。願意付這個代價的人，才配得上那段那麼好的陪伴。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把「我怎麼還走不出來」normalize 成「我愛得夠深」，適合對自責復原太慢的飼主，也適合寫進慰問卡
variations: 悲傷不是你太脆弱，是你太用力愛過。愛有多深，這道口子就有多深，這很公平。
如果可以不痛，代價是從來沒愛過牠。你會怎麼選？我猜，你還是會選現在這樣痛著的自己。

en.content: It hurts this much because you truly loved them. There's no shortcut through this pain, no fast-forward, because the pain is just love — wearing a shape that's hard to carry right now. So don't rush to 'get better,' and don't fake being fine. Every tear you're crying is you settling the bill for years of love. Only someone willing to pay that price ever deserved company that good.
en.editorNote: Normalizes 'why am I not over this yet' into 'I loved deeply'; for owners blaming themselves for slow healing, and works in a sympathy card
variations: Grief isn't you being weak. It's you having loved hard. The wound runs exactly as deep as the love — and that's fair.
The only way to skip the pain was to never have loved them at all. Which would you pick? My guess is you'd still choose the version of you that's hurting right now.

items.sourceNote: 「久病照護後鬆一口氣的罪惡感」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 陪牠走到最後那段日子，你半夜爬起來換尿墊、算著幾點餵藥、看著牠一天比一天虛弱。牠走的那一刻，你哭，但心裡有一個角落，其實鬆了一口氣——然後你為這口氣，恨自己恨得要命。可是我想告訴你：那口氣不代表你不愛牠，那只代表你太累了，也代表你終於不用再看牠受苦。愛和解脫，是可以同時存在的。你沒有錯。
zh-tw.editorNote: 處理長期照護後那種很少人敢講的「鬆一口氣的罪惡感」，替飼主命名並赦免這種複雜情緒
variations: 你不是因為牠走了而鬆一口氣，你是因為牠終於不痛了而鬆一口氣。這兩件事，差很多。
累到想放手，跟不愛，是兩回事。你陪牠撐到了最後一刻，這件事本身，就是最深的愛。

en.content: In those last days you got up at 3am to change the pads, timed every dose, watched them grow weaker by the day. The moment they went, you cried — but some corner of you felt relief. And then you hated yourself for that breath of relief. But here's what I want you to hear: that relief doesn't mean you loved them less. It means you were exhausted, and it means you finally don't have to watch them suffer. Love and release can live in the same moment. You did nothing wrong.
en.editorNote: Addresses the rarely-spoken 'guilt of relief' after long-term caregiving; names the complicated feeling for the owner and absolves it
variations: You didn't feel relief that they were gone. You felt relief that they finally weren't in pain. Those two things are worlds apart.
Being too tired to keep going is not the same as not loving them. You stayed until the very last second — and that, by itself, is the deepest kind of love.

items.sourceNote: 「愛的風險是失去，你還會再選一次嗎」frame，原創改寫（Hilary Stanton Zunin 意象改寫）

zh-tw.content: 有人問：如果早知道結局會這麼痛，你還會養牠嗎？你心裡其實一秒就有答案。會，我還是會在那個籠子前蹲下來，還是會帶牠回家，還是會愛牠愛到現在這樣心碎。因為就算連結局一起算進去，那些一起賴在沙發上、一起淋雨、一起長大的日子，還是值得。愛的風險本來就是失去，但比起從沒愛過，這種痛，我甘願。
zh-tw.editorNote: 用「你還會再選一次嗎」這個問句把悲傷 reframe 成「這段愛值得」，適合週年紀念或走過一段時間後回望
variations: 會痛，是因為當初值得。如果重來一次，我還是會走向那隻在角落看著我的小毛球。
我不後悔愛牠，一秒都不。我只後悔時間太短。但太短的幸福，還是幸福。

en.content: Someone asks: if you'd known the ending would hurt this much, would you still have taken them in? And honestly, you know the answer in a heartbeat. Yes. I'd still crouch down at that kennel, still bring them home, still love them all the way to this heartbreak. Because even counting the ending, those days lazing on the couch, getting caught in the rain, growing up side by side — they were worth it. The risk of love was always loss. But next to never having loved at all, this pain? I'd take it, gladly.
en.editorNote: Uses the 'would you choose it again?' question to reframe grief as 'this love was worth it'; good for an anniversary or looking back after some time has passed
variations: It hurts because it was worth it. If I could do it over, I'd still walk straight toward that little furball watching me from the corner.
I don't regret loving them, not for a second. I only regret how short the time was. But happiness that's too short is still happiness.

items.sourceNote: 兒童哀傷輔導：用「身體停止運作」而非「睡著了」的誠實語言，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 跟孩子解釋的時候，別說牠「睡著了」或「去很遠的地方旅行」——孩子會一直等牠醒來、等牠回家。你可以蹲下來，牽著他的手說：牠的身體太累了，停下來了，牠不會再痛，也不會再回來了，但我們可以一直想牠。誠實，反而是最溫柔的保護。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給要向孩子開口的家長，提醒別用「睡著了／去旅行」的委婉說法以免孩子誤解，適合親子共讀或家長私訊參考
variations: 孩子問「牠什麼時候回來」，你不用騙他。你可以說：牠不會回來了，但牠有多愛你，一點都不會不見。
可以哭給孩子看。讓他知道難過是正常的，也讓他知道，難過是因為我們真的很愛牠。

en.content: When you explain it to a child, don't say the pet "fell asleep" or "went on a long trip" — they'll keep waiting for it to wake up, keep watching the door. Crouch down, hold their hand, and say: their body got too tired and stopped working, they won't hurt anymore, and they won't come back — but we can keep loving them and missing them for as long as we want. Honesty is actually the gentlest way to protect them.
en.editorNote: For a parent who has to break the news to a child; warns against 'asleep/on a trip' euphemisms that confuse kids. Good for reading together or as a reference in a DM to a grieving parent
variations: When they ask 'when is it coming back,' you don't have to lie. You can say: it isn't coming back — but how much it loved you, that part never goes anywhere.
It's okay to cry in front of your kid. Let them see that sad is normal, and that we're sad because we really, really loved them.

items.sourceNote: 獸醫語錄「該慶幸是他先離開，悲傷由我們承擔」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 有個獸醫說過一句話，我一直記著：還好是牠先走。因為所有的想念、所有的難過，都由我們扛，而不是留給那個傻傻的牠，去承受找不到你的那種慌。牠不懂什麼叫生老病死，牠只會一直等、一直等。所以這份痛我來揹，讓牠什麼都不用怕，這樣，剛剛好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把「白髮人送黑髮人」式的自責 reframe 成「由我承擔，讓牠免於恐懼」的溫柔，適合安慰覺得「捨不得放手」的飼主
variations: 如果先走的是我，牠會在門口等到天荒地老，等到不懂為什麼你再也沒回來。所以，這次換我來想牠，值得。
牠不用學會失去，這件事，是我能給牠最後的溫柔。

en.content: A vet once said something I've held onto ever since: it's a mercy they went first. Because all the missing, all the ache — we're the ones who carry it, not that trusting little soul who'd never understand why you stopped coming home. They don't know what aging and dying mean. They'd just wait, and wait, and wait. So let me be the one to hold this pain. Let them never have to be afraid of anything. That's how it should be.
en.editorNote: Reframes the guilt of 'outliving them' into the tenderness of 'I carry the grief so they never had to feel loss.' Good for comforting an owner who couldn't bear to let go
variations: If I'd gone first, they'd have waited at the door forever, never understanding why you didn't come back. So this time, let me be the one who misses. It's worth it.
They never had to learn what losing someone feels like. That's the last kindness I got to give them.

items.sourceNote: 網友「最想念的一件事」：濕鼻子叫起床、床邊的位置，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 最想念的，其實不是什麼大事。是每天早上那顆濕濕的鼻子頂我的手，逼我起床；是我一坐下，牠就自動來佔我大腿；是半夜翻身，腳邊那團溫溫的重量還在。牠走了以後，家還是那個家，只是床變得好大，早上安靜得刺耳。原來最痛的，是那些習慣成自然、沒來得及好好記住的小事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 聚焦「失去日常小細節」的具體想念，貓飼主特別有共鳴，適合週年或某個突然被觸動的深夜寫下
variations: 牠留下的空位，比整個房間還大。
我還是會下意識留一口飯、留半邊床。身體比腦袋更晚知道，牠不在了。

en.content: What I miss most isn't anything big. It's the wet little nose nudging my hand awake every morning. It's the way they'd claim my lap the second I sat down. It's the warm weight against my feet when I rolled over at 3am. After they were gone, the house was still the house — the bed just got so big, and the mornings got loud with quiet. Turns out the sharpest ache is the tiny stuff, the things that became habit before I ever thought to memorize them.
en.editorNote: Zooms in on missing the small daily rituals; hits especially hard for cat owners. Good for an anniversary or a late night when it suddenly catches up with you
variations: The empty spot they left is bigger than the whole room.
I still catch myself leaving a bite of food, saving half the bed. The body figures it out slower than the mind — that they're gone.

items.sourceNote: 紀念盒 ritual：項圈、玩具、腳印收進盒子，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 找一個盒子，把牠的項圈放進去，還有那顆咬到脫線的玩具、剪下來的一小撮毛、蓋在紙上的腳印。想牠的時候，就把盒子打開。這不是為了忘記，剛好相反——是給思念一個家，讓牠有地方可以放，不用整天壓在胸口。愛沒有結束，只是換了一種收藏的方式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 提供具體的「紀念盒」做法，把抽象的悲傷轉成可以動手做的儀式，適合分享給不知如何開始告別的飼主或陪孩子一起做
variations: 把牠的名牌串在鑰匙圈上，這樣每天出門，牠都還跟著你。
思念太重的時候，就給它一個盒子、一個角落、一個名字。有地方放，就比較揹得動。

en.content: Find a box. Put their collar in it — and the toy they chewed to threads, a little snip of fur, a paw print pressed into paper. When you miss them, open the box. This isn't about forgetting; it's the opposite. It's giving your grief a home, somewhere to live, so it doesn't have to sit on your chest all day long. The love didn't end. You're just keeping it a different way.
en.editorNote: Offers a concrete 'memory box' ritual, turning abstract grief into something you can make with your hands. Good to share with someone who doesn't know how to start saying goodbye, or to do alongside a child
variations: Thread their name tag onto your keyring. That way they're still with you every time you walk out the door.
When the missing gets too heavy, give it a box, a corner, a name. Once it has somewhere to live, it's easier to carry.

items.sourceNote: 網友「趴在門口等我的畫面永遠烙印」frame，狗飼主視角，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 每次我回家，鑰匙都還沒轉開，就聽見門後那陣爪子撞地板的聲音，那麼急，好像我離開了一輩子。現在門後安安靜靜的，我卻還是會在開門那一秒愣一下。牠趴在門口等我的樣子，我大概一輩子都忘不了。原來被人這樣毫無保留地等著回家，是這麼奢侈的一件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 捕捉狗飼主特有的「開門迎接」記憶，用日常畫面承載思念，適合貼在玄關、寫進紀念文或某個下班回到空屋的夜晚
variations: 牠這輩子最重要的行程，就是等我回家。這件事，我到現在才懂有多珍貴。
門後不再有腳步聲了。但只要我還記得那個聲音，牠就還在等我。

en.content: Every time I came home, before the key even turned, I'd hear it — claws scrambling across the floor behind the door, so frantic, like I'd been gone a lifetime. Now it's silent back there, and still I freeze for a second every time I open it. The way they'd lie waiting by that door — I don't think I'll ever forget it. Turns out being waited for like that, so completely, with nothing held back, is one of the most extravagant things in the world.
en.editorNote: Captures the dog owner's signature 'welcome at the door' memory, carrying grief through an everyday image. Good for the entryway, a memorial note, or a night you come home to an empty house
variations: The most important thing on their whole schedule was waiting for me to come home. I only get how precious that was now.
There are no more footsteps behind the door. But as long as I remember the sound, they're still there waiting for me.

items.sourceNote: 「勿講一句安慰話」frame，陪伴喪寵者視角，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 如果身邊有人的毛孩剛走了，別急著說「再養一隻就好」。牠不是壞掉的家電，換一台就沒事。你只要坐在他旁邊，聽他講那些「牠以前都會怎樣怎樣」，讓他哭，讓他一直講同一段回憶都沒關係。你不用把他修好，你只要別讓他一個人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫給「想安慰卻怕說錯話」的親友，點出喪寵者要的是聆聽而非建議，適合轉發給對方的家人或另一半
variations: 他不需要你給答案，他需要你留下來。
最好的安慰有時候一句話都不用，只要遞一張衛生紙，然後陪著。

en.content: If someone you love just lost their pet, don't rush to say "you can always get another one." It wasn't a broken appliance you swap out. Just sit next to them. Let them tell you all the little "they used to do this" stories, let them cry, let them loop the same memory a hundred times. You don't have to fix them. You just have to not let them be alone.
en.editorNote: For the friend who wants to help but is scared of saying the wrong thing — grieving people need listening, not advice. Good to forward to a partner or family member
variations: They don't need you to have an answer. They need you to stay.
Sometimes the best comfort has no words in it at all — just a tissue handed over, and you, still there.

items.sourceNote: 寵物溝通師「毛孩不希望你背著罪惡感活」frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你一直在想「如果那天早點帶牠去看醫生就好了」。但牠從來沒有一秒鐘怪過你。在牠心裡，你是那個會回家、會餵飯、會摸摸牠頭的全世界。牠最不想看到的，就是你背著這份罪惡感過完剩下的日子。牠已經放下了，換你了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 專門承接喪寵後最折磨人的自責情緒，把「牠不會怪你」講清楚，適合私訊給正在鑽牛角尖的飼主
variations: 你已經做到最好了。愛得不夠從來不是你的問題，你只是捨不得。
牠要的不是一個完美的主人，是你。而你一直都在。

en.content: You keep replaying it — "if only I'd taken them to the vet a day sooner." But they never blamed you, not for one second. In their eyes you were the whole world: the one who came home, filled the bowl, scratched behind their ears. The last thing they'd ever want is for you to spend the rest of your days carrying this guilt. They've already let it go. Now it's your turn.
en.editorNote: Made to hold the cruelest part of pet grief — the self-blame — and say plainly that they don't blame you. Good as a private message to someone spiraling
variations: You did the best anyone could. Loving too little was never the problem — you just couldn't bear to let go.
They never needed a perfect owner. They needed you. And you were always there.

items.sourceNote: 彩虹橋重逢 frame，restored to health 意象，徹底改寫

zh-tw.content: 橋的那一端沒有病痛，沒有針，也沒有那間你們一起去了太多次的醫院。牠的腿又能跑了，眼睛又亮了，追著蝴蝶穿過整片草地。牠什麼都不缺，只差一件事——還在等你。所以你要好好過，不是為了忘記牠，是為了有一天走過那座橋的時候，能笑著讓牠撲進懷裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 改寫彩虹橋「病痛痊癒、原地等待」的核心意象，把它變成勸生者好好活的理由，適合骨灰罈卡片或週年紀念文
variations: 牠在那頭跑得飛快，但每隔一陣子就會回頭看橋，看你來了沒。
牠不是不見了，是先過去把最好的位置佔好，等你。

en.content: On the other side of the bridge there's no pain, no needles, none of that clinic you two went to one too many times. Their legs work again, their eyes are bright again, chasing butterflies clear across the meadow. They have everything now — except one thing. They're still waiting for you. So live well. Not to forget them, but so that when you finally cross that bridge, you can laugh as they leap into your arms.
en.editorNote: Reworks the Rainbow Bridge core image — healed and waiting — into a reason for the living to keep going well. Fits an urn card or an anniversary post
variations: They run flat-out over there, but every little while they glance back at the bridge, checking if you've come yet.
They're not gone. They just went ahead to save the best spot, and they're waiting.

items.sourceNote: 「grief forever, rebuild around the loss」名言 frame，徹底改寫

zh-tw.content: 沒有人會真的「走出來」。你不會有一天醒來就不痛了。你只是慢慢學會怎麼帶著這個洞繼續生活——它不會補起來，但你會在它周圍長出新的自己。有一天你會發現，想到牠的時候，嘴角先笑了，眼淚才慢半拍跟上。那不是你忘了牠，那是思念終於變得溫柔。
zh-tw.editorNote: 誠實不灌雞湯地講「悲傷不會消失、只會學會共處」，適合喪寵一段時間後仍走不出來、被旁人催「該放下了」的飼主
variations: 痛不會變小，是你會慢慢長大到裝得下它。
別人叫你放下的時候，你可以只是把牠放進心裡更深的地方，繼續帶著走。

en.content: Nobody really "gets over" it. You won't wake up one day and find it stopped hurting. You just slowly learn how to live around the hole — it never fills in, but you grow a new version of yourself around its edges. And one day you'll notice that when they cross your mind, the smile comes first and the tears run a beat behind. That's not you forgetting them. That's the missing finally turning gentle.
en.editorNote: Honest, not sugar-coated — grief doesn't vanish, you learn to carry it. For someone still hurting a while later, being told by others it's 'time to move on'
variations: The pain doesn't shrink. You just slowly grow big enough to hold it.
When people tell you to let go, you're allowed to just tuck them deeper into your heart and keep walking.

items.sourceNote: 貓飼主視角，「牠選了離你最近的位置離開」frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 貓不太會把愛講出來，牠只是每天默默挑一個離你最近的位置窩著。你打電腦，牠就趴在鍵盤旁；你睡覺，牠就佔住你腳邊那一角。現在那些位置都空了，我才懂——牠一輩子都在用「靠近你」這件事，偷偷說著牠有多愛你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 捕捉貓特有的「不黏卻總在身邊」的愛，用空掉的固定位置承載思念，適合貓飼主的紀念貼文或玄關小卡
variations: 牠不會跑來討抱，但你走到哪，牠的視線就跟到哪。
貓的愛都藏在距離裡。牠選的每一個位置，都剛好是能看著你的地方。

en.content: Cats don't say love out loud. They just quietly pick, every single day, the spot closest to you and curl up there. You work, they sprawl by the keyboard; you sleep, they claim the corner by your feet. Now all those spots sit empty, and only now do I understand — their whole life, just by staying near you, they were secretly telling you how much they loved you.
en.editorNote: Captures the cat-specific love — aloof but always nearby — carrying grief through the now-empty regular spots. For a cat owner's memorial post or an entryway card
variations: They'd never come running for a cuddle, but wherever you went, their eyes followed.
A cat keeps its love in the distance it chooses. Every spot they picked was one where they could watch you.

items.sourceNote: 家中其他寵物也會哀傷的觀察，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 家裡剩下的那隻，這幾天一直走到門口聞一聞，再走回來趴著。牠不會問，但牠知道少了誰。我們兩個現在都在學同一件事：怎麼在一個少了牠的家裡，重新學會呼吸。有時候我抱著牠哭，牠也不掙扎，就讓我抱著。原來悲傷也是可以分著扛的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫給多寵家庭，把「另一隻毛孩也在難過」這件常被忽略的事說出來，適合貼文或給同樣有多隻寵物的朋友
variations: 牠沒有在等我開飯，牠在等那個永遠不會再進門的身影。
我以為只有我在難過，直到我看見牠對著空掉的那張墊子聞了很久。

en.content: The one still here keeps walking to the door, sniffing, and coming back to lie down. She can't ask, but she knows who's missing. The two of us are learning the same thing right now: how to breathe again in a house that's short one. Sometimes I hold her and cry and she doesn't squirm — she just lets me. Turns out grief can be carried between two.
en.editorNote: For multi-pet homes, naming the often-overlooked fact that the surviving pet is grieving too. Works as a post or a note to a friend with other animals at home
variations: She isn't waiting for dinner. She's waiting for someone who isn't coming through that door again.
I thought I was the only one hurting, until I watched her stand over that empty bed and just breathe it in.

items.sourceNote: 獸醫分享「九成飼主不敢在場，寵物最後在找主人」討論串，改寫為安撫不敢在場者的角度

zh-tw.content: 你說你那天沒能撐住，在門外哭到腿軟，沒有陪牠走完最後那幾分鐘。可是牠認得你的味道，那條牠睡了好幾年的小被子就蓋在牠身上。牠這輩子有幾千個日子是你陪的，別用最後那幾分鐘，去否定前面那幾千天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 專門承接「安樂死時不敢在場」的深層愧疚，適合私訊給正在反覆責備自己的飼主，或安樂後幾天的關心訊息
variations: 你不是逃走，你只是已經痛到站不住了。牠會懂的。
牠最後聞到的是家的味道，那是你給的。

en.content: You said you couldn't hold it together that day — you cried in the hallway until your legs gave out, and you weren't in the room for those last few minutes. But she knew your smell. That worn blanket she'd slept on for years was still over her. You gave her thousands of days. Don't let the last few minutes cancel out all of them.
en.editorNote: Written for the specific guilt of not being in the room at the end. Good as a private message to someone replaying it, or a check-in a few days after
variations: You didn't abandon her. You were already in too much pain to stand. She'd understand that.
The last thing she smelled was home, and home was something you gave her.

items.sourceNote: 節日與紀念儀式 frame，原創改寫為「第一個沒有牠的節日」

zh-tw.content: 今年是第一個沒有牠的過年。桌上還是那麼多菜，只是不會再有一雙眼睛從桌腳底下盯著我看。我還是夾了一塊肉放在小碟子裡，放在牠以前趴的位置。有人說這樣很傻，但我覺得，只要我還記得替牠留一份，牠就還在這個家的名單上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給第一次遇到節日的喪寵家庭，把「留一份給牠」的小儀式寫成思念的出口，適合節慶期間的貼文或發給同樣在過節難熬的朋友
variations: 每年多擺一副碗筷，是我維持牠還在的方式。
團圓的日子最難，因為少一個人的時候，桌子會突然變得好大。

en.content: This is the first holiday without him. The table's just as full, only now there's no pair of eyes staring up at me from under it. I still put a piece of meat on a little dish and set it where he used to lie. People say that's silly. But as long as I keep saving him a portion, he's still on this family's list.
en.editorNote: For a family facing their first holiday after the loss, turning the small ritual of 'setting a place' into somewhere the grief can go. Fits a holiday post or a message to a friend dreading the same day
variations: Setting one extra bowl every year is how I keep him here.
The gathering days are the hardest, because one missing body makes the whole table feel enormous.

items.sourceNote: 夢見逝去寵物的常見經驗，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 昨晚夢到牠了。沒有什麼特別的劇情，就是牠跳上床，繞了兩圈，靠著我的背躺下來，跟以前一模一樣。醒來的時候枕頭是濕的，可是心裡沒有以前那麼緊了。我不知道那是不是真的牠來看我，但那個重量太真實了，真實到我願意相信。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫夢見毛孩的體驗，不下定論、只留下溫柔的可能性，適合半夜睡不著時的貼文或回覆說「我夢到牠了」的朋友
variations: 夢裡牠什麼都沒說，只是把頭靠過來，好像在說牠過得很好。
有人說那只是大腦在整理回憶。可是回憶不會有溫度，那晚牠是暖的。

en.content: I dreamed about him last night. Nothing dramatic — he just hopped onto the bed, turned around twice, and settled against my back exactly the way he always did. I woke up with a wet pillow, but my chest wasn't as tight as it usually is. I don't know if that was really him coming by. But the weight of him felt so real that I'm willing to believe it was.
en.editorNote: About dreaming of a pet who's gone — leaves the question open instead of answering it. For a sleepless-night post, or replying to a friend who says 'I dreamed about her'
variations: He didn't say anything in the dream. He just leaned his head in, like he was telling me he's okay.
People say it's just your brain filing memories. But memories don't have body heat, and that night he was warm.

items.sourceNote: 「說出寵物的名字」是最好的安慰 frame，改寫為給旁人的行動指引

zh-tw.content: 想安慰牠的家人，其實不需要什麼漂亮的話。你只要叫出牠的名字就好——「我一直記得咪咪那個歪頭的樣子」。因為大家都不敢提，怕戳到傷口，久了之後最讓人難過的，反而是牠好像從所有人的對話裡消失了。你提起牠，等於幫牠在這個世界上多留一天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給不知道怎麼開口的旁人：具體做法是說出寵物的名字和一個回憶，適合分享給想關心朋友卻怕說錯話的人
variations: 不用說「別難過」，說「我也很想牠」就好。
一週後再傳一次訊息，比當天說一百句安慰更有用。

en.content: You don't need the perfect words to comfort their family. Just say the name — "I still think about the way Mimi used to tilt her head." Everyone tiptoes around it, afraid of reopening the wound, and after a while the worst part is that she seems to have vanished from every conversation. Saying her name keeps her in the world one more day.
en.editorNote: For the friend who doesn't know what to say: the concrete move is naming the pet and offering one memory. Share with someone afraid of saying the wrong thing
variations: Skip "don't be sad." Try "I miss him too."
A second message a week later does more than a hundred kind words on day one.

items.sourceNote: 「宅配訂閱飼料在離世後才寄到」具體物件 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 門口放著一箱飼料。是三個月前設定的自動宅配，機器不會知道你已經先走了。我抱著箱子在門口站了很久，最後沒退貨——我把它捐去了收容所，跟工作人員說，這是我家一隻很挑食的狗，用牠的份，去餵一隻願意乖乖吃飯的孩子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫在整理遺物、收到定期宅配的貼文裡；把「無法取消的日常」轉成一個溫柔的動作，不落入純粹悲傷
variations: 那箱飼料我一直沒拆。它證明了，直到上個月，我都還準備好好餵你很久很久。
取消訂閱的那一刻，比想像中還難按下去。按下去，就好像我也承認了。

en.content: There's a box of food at the door. An auto-delivery I set up three months ago — the system has no way of knowing you left first. I stood there holding it for a long time, then didn't send it back. I donated it to the shelter and told them: this was for a very picky dog of mine. Use his share to feed a kid who'll actually eat.
en.editorNote: For a post about sorting a pet's things or getting a subscription box after the loss; turns 'the routine you can't cancel' into a gentle act instead of pure grief
variations: I never opened that box. It's proof that as of last month, I was still planning to feed you for a long, long time.
Hitting 'cancel subscription' was harder than I expected. Pressing it felt like admitting it too.

items.sourceNote: 「手機鎖定畫面還是牠」具體物件 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 我的手機鎖定畫面還是你。一天不知道要解鎖幾十次，也就等於一天要跟你打幾十次照面。朋友小心翼翼地問，要不要換掉，會不會每次看到都難過。我想了想，說不用——難過歸難過，可是能一天看你這麼多次的機會，我還捨不得放掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合社群貼文或回覆「要不要換手機桌布」的關心；把「不換」講成一種主動的選擇，而不是走不出來
variations: 有時候會愣個半秒才想起來，然後笑一下，再滑開。這半秒，是我一天裡最想留住的。
等哪天我看著你不再鼻酸，只剩下想笑，我再換。現在還不急。

en.content: My lock screen is still you. I unlock this phone a few dozen times a day, which means a few dozen times a day I get to see your face. A friend asked, gently, whether I should change it — doesn't it hurt every time. I thought about it and said no. It does hurt. But the chance to see you that many times a day, I'm not ready to give up.
en.editorNote: For a social post or replying to a 'should you change your wallpaper' check-in; frames keeping it as an active choice, not being stuck
variations: Sometimes I blank for half a second before I remember, then I smile and swipe. That half-second is the part of the day I most want to keep.
The day I can look at you without the sting — just the smile — I'll change it. No rush yet.

items.sourceNote: 華人祭祀文化（清明/中元擺一副碗筷）frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 今年拜拜，我在供桌角落多擺了一個小碗，裝了你最愛的那款肉泥。長輩皺眉說哪有人祭拜寵物的，我沒爭。我只是覺得，一家人團聚的日子，本來就不該漏掉任何一個成員。你也是走過我們家門、睡過我們家床、吃過年夜飯桌邊掉下來那塊肉的人啊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合清明、中元或過年時，想把毛孩納入家庭祭祀卻怕被長輩念的人；重點在「牠是家人」的正當性
variations: 香點三炷，我分你一炷。你不用學規矩，聞到味道，知道我在叫你回家吃飯就好。
別人說牠只是隻狗，不能上供桌。可我們家的規矩，向來是愛過的都算數。

en.content: At the family offering this year, I set a small bowl in the corner of the altar with your favorite paste in it. An elder frowned — who makes offerings to a pet. I didn't argue. I just feel that on the day a family reunites, you don't leave anyone off the table. You walked through this door too, slept in these beds, ate the scraps that fell by your seat at New Year's dinner.
en.editorNote: For Qingming, Ghost Month, or Lunar New Year, for someone who wants to include their pet in family remembrance despite pushback; centers on 'they were family'
variations: Three sticks of incense lit; one of them is yours. You don't need to know the rituals — just smell it and know I'm calling you home for dinner.
They said it's just a dog, it doesn't belong on the altar. But in our house the rule has always been: whoever we loved, counts.

items.sourceNote: 「寵物沒有喪假」職場處境 frame，改寫為給旁人的行動指引

zh-tw.content: 同事今天請了一天假，理由寫「身體不適」。其實我知道，昨晚走的是陪了他十四年的貓。沒有一種假叫喪寵假，所以他只能把這場告別，塞進一格病假裡偷偷過完。他回來上班那天，別問他好點沒——就走過去輕輕說一句：「昨天辛苦了，牠很幸運有你。」然後把那杯他常喝的咖啡，默默放到他桌上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給主管或同事：具體做法是不戳破那格病假、用一句話承認他的傷痛；適合分享給想關心同事又怕逾矩的人
variations: 不用說「不過是隻貓」，說「牠陪了你十四年，這不是小事」就好。
他不需要你幫他分攤工作，他需要有人知道，他今天笑得很勉強。

en.content: A coworker took a day off today. The reason on the form said 'not feeling well.' But I know it was the cat who'd been with him fourteen years that left last night. There's no such thing as pet bereavement leave, so he had to fold this whole goodbye into a single sick day and get through it quietly. When he's back, don't ask if he's feeling better — walk over and say softly, "Yesterday was hard. He was lucky to have you." Then set his usual coffee on his desk without a word.
en.editorNote: For a manager or coworker: the concrete move is not exposing the sick day and acknowledging the loss in one line; share with someone who wants to support a colleague without overstepping
variations: Skip 'it was just a cat.' Try 'fourteen years is not a small thing.'
He doesn't need you to cover his workload. He needs someone to notice that today's smile is costing him something.

items.sourceNote: 「感官型悲傷」phantom sounds／項圈鈴鐺聲，改寫為安慰半夜聽見聲音的人

zh-tw.content: 家裡最安靜的，不是沒有你的叫聲，是沒有你的「動靜」。以前不用回頭也知道你在——項圈的鈴鐺叮一聲、指甲在木地板上答答走過、趴下來那口滿足的長嘆。現在這些全部消失了，安靜得我半夜會突然醒過來，豎起耳朵，等一個再也不會響的聲音。如果你也在深夜聽見那熟悉的鈴鐺，別急著否認——那不是幻覺，那是愛還沒學會怎麼安靜下來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給「明明知道牠走了，卻還一直豎耳朵聽」的人；點出感官型悲傷是正常的，不是自己瘋了
variations: 我不是想念某一個聲音，我是想念那個「有你在」的整個背景音。
他們說那只是幻聽。我寧願相信，是你回來確認我有沒有好好睡。

en.content: The quietest thing about the house isn't the missing bark — it's the missing motion of you. I never had to turn around to know you were there: the jingle of the tag, nails clicking across the wood floor, that long satisfied sigh as you flopped down. All of it is gone now, quiet enough that I wake at 2am with my ears straining, waiting for a sound that will never come again. If you catch yourself listening for that familiar jingle late at night, don't rush to call it nothing — it isn't a glitch. It's love that hasn't figured out how to go quiet yet.
en.editorNote: For the person who knows their pet is gone but still keeps listening for them; names sensory grief as normal, not a sign you're losing it
variations: I don't miss one specific sound. I miss the whole background hum of you being here.
They say it's just my mind filling the silence. I'd rather believe you came back to check I was sleeping okay.

items.sourceNote: 寄養／中途動物離世的獨特悲傷，改寫為給中途志工的自我安慰

zh-tw.content: 你只在我家住了三個禮拜。我從一開始就知道，我不是你的終點——我只是那個負責在半路上，讓你相信人類還值得信任的人。可是你沒等到那個家，就在我懷裡走了。有人說「反正又不是你的狗，別太難過」，可是那三個禮拜，餵你、幫你點眼藥、半夜陪你的，是我。愛不會因為時間短就打折。你這一生最後感受到的是被抱著、被叫名字——這件事，我這輩子都會記得是我給你的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給中途／寄養志工：對抗「又不是你的寵物，何必這麼傷心」這種否定；肯定短暫的照顧也是完整的愛
variations: 我沒能把你送到那個家，可是我讓你在走之前，先嚐過一次「被愛」是什麼味道。
下一隻我還是會接。不是因為不痛，是因為你讓我知道，這件事值得痛。

en.content: You only lived at my place for three weeks. I knew from day one I wasn't your destination — I was just the person whose job was to convince you, halfway through, that humans were still worth trusting. But you never made it to that forever home. You left in my arms instead. People say, "It wasn't even your dog, don't take it so hard." But for those three weeks, the one who fed you, put in your eye drops, sat up with you at 3am — that was me. Love doesn't get discounted for being short. The last thing you ever felt was being held and called by name, and I will spend the rest of my life knowing that was mine to give you.
en.editorNote: For fosters and rescue volunteers: pushes back on 'it wasn't even your pet, why so upset'; affirms that short-term care is still complete love
variations: I couldn't get you to that home. But I made sure you tasted what being loved felt like before you went.
I'll still take the next one in. Not because it doesn't hurt — because you taught me it's worth the hurt.

items.sourceNote: 感謝陪伴善終的獸醫團隊，改寫為一封寫給醫療團隊的謝卡文字

zh-tw.content: 這封是寫給那天在場的醫生和護理師的。謝謝你們沒有把牠當成當天的第幾號病例。你蹲下來，先讓牠聞了聞你的手，才慢慢靠近；你把燈調暗、聲音放到最輕；最後那一針推之前，你還低頭跟牠說了句「乖，不痛囉」。我當時哭到說不出話，可是我全都看在眼裡。你們每天都要陪別人走這一段，我不知道你們怎麼撐的——但請你們記得，有一個哭到不成人形的家長，這輩子都會感謝你們，讓牠走得那麼有尊嚴。
zh-tw.editorNote: 可直接抄進給獸醫院的謝卡或 Google 評論；示範怎麼具體感謝陪伴善終的醫療團隊，而不只是「謝謝你們」
variations: 你大可以公事公辦，但你選擇蹲下來，先跟牠說話。這個選擇，我記一輩子。
你們每天送走別人家的寶貝，還能保持這麼溫柔——謝謝你們沒有讓自己麻木。

en.content: This one's for the vet and the tech who were in the room that day. Thank you for not treating him like case number whatever on your schedule. You crouched down and let him sniff your hand before you came closer; you dimmed the lights and dropped your voice to almost nothing; and right before that last injection, you leaned in and told him, "Good boy, no more hurting." I was crying too hard to speak, but I saw every bit of it. You do this walk with someone else's family every single day — I don't know how you carry it — but please know there's one parent, an absolute wreck that afternoon, who will be grateful for the rest of their life that you let him go with that much dignity.
en.editorNote: Ready to copy into a thank-you card or Google review for the clinic; models how to thank an end-of-life vet team specifically, not just 'thanks for everything'
variations: You could have kept it clinical. You chose to crouch down and talk to him first. I'll remember that choice forever.
You send other people's babies off every day and still stay this gentle — thank you for not letting yourselves go numb.

items.sourceNote: 醫療費 vs 保守治療的罪惡感，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你半夜偷偷算過那張估價單，最後選了保守的那條路。現在你一直在想，如果當初咬牙做了那個手術、砸下那筆錢，牠是不是還在。我想跟你說：愛牠，從來不是用你花了多少錢來算的。你在能力範圍裡，給了牠最不痛的選擇——那不是放棄，那是另一種捨不得。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些因為醫療費用做了保守決定、事後陷入「錢沒花夠」自責的飼主，適合私訊或安慰卡
variations: 帳單上的數字，量不出你對牠的愛。你在現實裡替牠選了最不受苦的那條路，這已經很勇敢了。

en.content: You did the math on that estimate at 2am and chose the gentler road. Now you keep wondering — if you'd found the money, done the surgery, would you still have them. Here's the truth: love was never measured by the size of the bill. Inside what you had, you gave them the least painful choice. That's not giving up. That's love wearing its hardest face.
en.editorNote: For owners who made a cost-driven treatment decision and are now stuck on 'I should have spent more'; good as a private message or card
variations: The number on that invoice never measured how much you loved them. You chose the path that spared them the most suffering, within what was real. That took courage.

items.sourceNote: 毛孩是逝去親人留下的、雙重失落，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你是我媽走之前，硬塞到我懷裡的。這些年我以為是我在養你，後來才發現，是你替她繼續陪著我。所以你走的那天，我哭得比誰都久——因為我知道，這一次，是真的把她也一起送走了。謝謝你幫她，多陪了我這麼多年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些毛孩是逝去親人留下的飼主，失去牠等於再失去那個人一次，是很少被說出口的雙重失落
variations: 你是外婆留給我的最後一點溫度。這些年你窩在我腿上的時候，我總覺得她也在。現在你走了，我才敢承認，我是真的第二次失去她了。

en.content: My mom pressed you into my arms before she went. All these years I thought I was the one raising you — turns out you were the one staying, on her behalf. So the day you left, I cried longer than anyone understood. Because I knew: this time, I was finally letting go of her too. Thank you for holding her place this long.
en.editorNote: For someone whose pet was left behind by a departed loved one; losing the pet is losing that person a second time — a rarely-voiced double grief
variations: You were the last bit of warmth my grandmother left me. Every time you curled up on my lap, it felt like she was still here. Now that you're gone, I can finally admit it — I've lost her twice.

items.sourceNote: 「你有養寵物嗎」的時態難題，原創

zh-tw.content: 最難的問題，往往是最沒惡意的那句：「你有養寵物嗎？」我卡在那半秒，不知道該用「有」還是「有過」。說「有過」，好像太快把你歸進過去；說「有」，又得解釋你已經不在了。後來我學會了回答：「有一隻狗，牠叫豆豆，是我這輩子最好的決定。」——不提時態，只提你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給失去毛孩後、面對陌生人日常寒暄卻不知如何回答的飼主，提供一個溫柔的說法
variations: 朋友介紹新同事，隨口問我家裡有沒有毛孩。我愣了一下，最後說：「有一隻貓，陪了我十六年。」我沒說牠已經走了——那一刻我只想好好講講牠，不想解釋。

en.content: The hardest question is usually the most harmless one: "Do you have any pets?" I freeze for half a second — is it "have" or "had"? Say "had," and I've filed you into the past too fast. Say "have," and I owe them the whole explanation. So I learned to answer: "I have a dog named Bean. Best decision I ever made." No tense. Just you.
en.editorNote: For someone navigating casual small talk after losing a pet, unsure how to answer; offers a gentle script
variations: A new coworker asked, just making conversation, whether I had any pets. I paused, then said: 'A cat. Sixteen years.' I didn't say she was gone — in that moment I just wanted to talk about her, not explain her.

items.sourceNote: 年輕毛孩早逝、白髮送黑髮的錯愕，原創

zh-tw.content: 你才三歲。這不在我們的約定裡。我以為我們還有十幾個春天可以浪費，還有好多條沒走過的路、好多個還沒到的生日。白髮送黑髮這種痛，沒想到養毛孩也會遇上。我沒有準備好，一點都沒有——可是那些我們硬生生被剪短的日子，每一天都是真的，誰都拿不走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給失去年輕、早逝毛孩的飼主，「還這麼小」「一切都太早」的錯愕與不公平感，不同於陪伴老衰的告別
variations: 別人的狗陪他們慢慢變老，你卻在最漂亮的年紀就停下了。我不甘心，也不明白。但我寧願愛你這短短幾年，也不要用一個更長、卻沒有你的人生去換。

en.content: You were only three. This wasn't the deal. I thought we still had a dozen springs to waste, so many roads unwalked, so many birthdays not yet reached. I never knew you could bury someone too young in this too. I wasn't ready — not even a little. But the days we had, the ones cut short without warning, every one of them was real. No one gets to take those.
en.editorNote: For someone who lost a young pet unexpectedly; the shock and unfairness of 'too soon,' distinct from saying goodbye to an old, failing pet
variations: Other people's dogs grow old with them. You stopped in your most beautiful year. I can't accept it, and I can't understand it. But I'd rather have loved you for these few short years than trade them for a longer life that never had you in it.

items.sourceNote: 失去情緒支柱／陪伴犬的雙重崩塌，原創

zh-tw.content: 別人失去的是一隻寵物，我失去的是我每天賴以撐住的那根柱子。你不只是陪我，你是我焦慮發作時抱著的那團溫度、是我不想起床時唯一的理由、是我撐過那幾年最黑的日子那個沉默的隊友。現在你走了，我不只要學會想你，還要重新學會，在沒有你的時候怎麼自己站穩。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給把毛孩當情緒支柱／陪伴犬的飼主，失去的是同伴，也是自己的支持系統，是雙重的崩塌
variations: 你是我的藥，也是我的家。恐慌來的時候，我把臉埋進你的毛裡數呼吸。現在那團毛不在了，我得學著自己數——這比想你還難。

en.content: Other people lost a pet. I lost the thing that held me up. You weren't just company — you were the warm weight I gripped through panic attacks, the only reason I got out of bed some days, the silent teammate who got me through the darkest years. Now you're gone, and I don't just have to learn to miss you. I have to relearn how to stand up on my own, without you under my hand.
en.editorNote: For someone whose pet was their emotional anchor or support animal; losing a companion and a coping system at once — a double collapse
variations: You were my medicine and my home. When the panic came, I'd bury my face in your fur and count my breaths. That fur is gone now, and I have to learn to count alone — which is harder than missing you.

items.sourceNote: 個別火化現場等候二至四小時＋撿骨流程，原創

zh-tw.content: 他們說要兩三個小時，我就在外面那排椅子上坐著。手機滑不下去，紙杯裡的咖啡也一口沒喝。旁邊的阿姨問我在等什麼，我說：「等我家的狗。」——這是我最後一次為你等了。你在門口等我下班等了十四年，這幾個小時，換我等你，一秒都不會走開。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給選擇個別火化、在現場等候的飼主，那段空白又難熬的兩三小時；也適合寫進告別紀念冊
variations: 師傅把小小的骨頭一片一片夾起來的時候，我發現我沒有哭。不是不難過，是那一刻我只想好好看著你，把最後這一段路也記清楚。

en.content: They said it would take a few hours, so I sat on the row of chairs outside. Couldn't scroll, couldn't touch the coffee. A woman beside me asked what I was waiting for. I said, "My dog." It was the last time I would ever wait for you. You spent fourteen years waiting by the door for me to come home. These few hours are mine to give back, and I'm not moving from this chair.
en.editorNote: For someone sitting through the wait at a private cremation; the blank, unbearable few hours nobody prepares you for
variations: When they lifted each small bone with the tongs, I realized I wasn't crying. Not because it didn't hurt. I just wanted to look at you properly, and remember this last part too.

items.sourceNote: 集體火化、沒有骨灰可帶回家的失落與自我和解，原創

zh-tw.content: 那時候手上真的沒有多的錢，我選了集體火化。沒有骨灰罈，也沒有一個可以去看你的地方。我為這件事偷偷難過了很久，覺得自己連最後一程都虧待了你。後來才想通：你本來就不住在罈子裡。你住在我每天走的那條路上、住在我到現在還是放很輕的關門聲裡、住在我心裡那個永遠不會租給別人的位置。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給因為經濟或其他考量選擇集體火化、沒有骨灰可以帶回家的飼主，減輕「連最後一程都做得不夠」的自責
variations: 我沒有你的骨灰，只有一小撮剪下來的毛和一條舊項圈，收在抽屜第二格。有人覺得那樣不夠慎重，但我知道，紀念從來不是在比誰的容器比較漂亮。

en.content: I didn't have the money then, so I chose the group cremation. No urn, no place to go and visit you. I carried that quietly for a long time, like I'd shortchanged you right at the end. It took me a while to understand: you were never going to live in a jar anyway. You live on the route I still walk, in the way I still close doors softly, in the spot inside me that I'll never rent out to anyone else.
en.editorNote: For someone who chose a communal cremation, for money or any other reason, and has no ashes to bring home; eases the 'I couldn't even do the last part right' guilt
variations: I don't have your ashes. I have a snip of fur and an old collar in the second drawer down. Someone once hinted that wasn't dignified enough. But remembering was never a contest over whose container is prettier.

items.sourceNote: 寵物告別式上可直接朗讀的送別文範本需求，原創

zh-tw.content: （告別式上可以直接唸的短文）今天我們送走的不是一隻寵物，是我們家的一份子。牠陪我們搬過三次家、陪我們熬過生病的那年、陪我們走過最難的那幾個月，什麼都沒要求，只要我們記得回家。米米，謝謝你選了我們家。你可以去玩了，去跑那種跑到肚子貼著地的快。我們會好好的。等到哪天我們老得走不動了，記得來門口接我們。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給要在寵物告別式上說幾句話、卻不知道從何開口的飼主；把名字和事件換成自己的即可，長度大約唸一分鐘
variations: （給不想長篇大論的人）謝謝你這十二年，每天都在門口等我。今天換我送你到門口。慢慢走，不用回頭，我們家永遠有你的位置。

en.content: (A short piece you can read aloud at the service.) What we're saying goodbye to today isn't a pet. It's family. She moved with us three times, sat through the year we were sick, carried us through the hardest months, and never asked for anything except that we remember to come home. Mimi — thank you for choosing this family. You can go and play now. Run the way you used to, belly low to the ground. We'll be okay. And when we're too old to walk far, come meet us at the door.
en.editorNote: For someone who has to speak at a pet's memorial and doesn't know how to start; swap in your own name and details, roughly a minute read aloud
variations: (For those who don't want to say much.) Thank you for twelve years of waiting by that door for me. Today I get to walk you to the door instead. Take your time. Don't look back. There will always be a place here that's yours.

items.sourceNote: 為毛孩設定的智慧家電在牠離世後仍持續運作的日常斷裂，原創

zh-tw.content: 自動餵食器早上七點還是「噠」了一聲，飼料掉進空碗裡，那個聲音現在聽起來特別大。掃地機器人一路暢通地開過客廳，沒有東西擋它，也沒有人追它。連寵物攝影機都還好好地對著那張小床拍，畫面裡什麼都沒有。那天我一個一個把它們關掉，比整理你的玩具還難。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給家裡還留著一堆為毛孩設定的智慧家電、每天定時提醒你牠不在的飼主；把「關掉它們」當成一次正式的告別
variations: 手機通知跳出來：「偵測到寵物活動」。我點開，是窗簾被風吹動。那三秒鐘，我是真的以為是你。

en.content: The automatic feeder still clicked at seven, and the kibble hit an empty bowl. That sound is so much louder now. The robot vacuum crosses the living room unobstructed — nothing in its way, nobody chasing it. The camera is still aimed at your little bed, streaming an empty frame all day. The afternoon I switched them off one by one was harder than packing up your toys.
en.editorNote: For someone whose home is still full of devices set up for a pet who's gone, each one announcing the absence on schedule; frames turning them off as its own goodbye
variations: My phone buzzed: "Pet motion detected." I opened it — just the curtain moving in the wind. For three whole seconds, I really thought it was you.

items.sourceNote: 給還在陪伴的毛孩：飼主總在鏡頭後面、幾乎沒有合照，原創

zh-tw.content: 去翻翻你的相簿。三千張裡面，牠大概佔了兩千八——睡覺的、打呵欠的、翻肚的，可是有你們兩個一起入鏡的，可能不到十張。因為你永遠站在鏡頭後面。等到哪天你很想找一張抱著牠的照片，你會很想揍現在的自己。今天就去拍一張。醜沒關係，糊掉也沒關係，重點是那張照片裡有你的手。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給毛孩還健康、還在身邊的人，一個現在就能做的小提醒；也很適合轉給正在養毛孩的朋友
variations: 順便錄一段十秒的影片，記得開聲音。照片留得住牠的樣子，只有影片留得住牠指甲踩在地板上那個喀喀的聲音。

en.content: Go look at your camera roll. Out of three thousand photos, maybe twenty-eight hundred are of them — sleeping, yawning, belly up. But photos with both of you in the frame? Probably fewer than ten. Because you're always the one behind the camera. Someday you'll go hunting for a picture of yourself holding them, and you'll want to shake your past self. Take one today. It can be unflattering. It can be blurry. What matters is that your hands are in it.
en.editorNote: For people whose pet is still healthy and still here; one small thing to do right now, and easy to pass along to a friend with a pet
variations: Record ten seconds of video while you're at it, sound on. Photos keep the face. Only video keeps the click of their nails crossing the floor.

items.sourceNote: 喪寵後被迫回歸日常、悲傷被輕視 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 喪假只有一天，可是你的世界又不是只塌一天。隔天照樣要進辦公室、開會、對客戶笑。沒人知道你午休是躲在樓梯間哭完、補個妝再上樓的。這種痛不會因為沒人看見，就比較輕。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給喪寵後被迫回歸日常、卻覺得沒人懂的人；也適合轉給主管，提醒體諒正在難過的同事
variations: 你不是玻璃心，是真的失去了一個家人。世界沒有為你停一秒，不代表你不能為牠停很久。

en.content: You get one day of bereavement leave, but your world didn't collapse for just one day. Next morning you're back at your desk, in meetings, smiling at clients. Nobody knows you spent your lunch break crying in the stairwell and fixing your face before heading back up. This pain isn't any lighter just because no one sees it.
en.editorNote: For people forced back to normal life after a loss and feeling unseen; also a nudge for managers to go easy on a grieving coworker
variations: You're not being dramatic. You lost family. The world didn't pause for a second — that doesn't mean you can't pause for a long while.

items.sourceNote: 臨終畫面反覆回放的罪惡感 frame，原創，反轉為「牠看的是你的臉」

zh-tw.content: 你一直放不下最後那一刻，反覆想自己是不是做錯了什麼。可是你知道嗎——牠到最後看的不是那些儀器、不是陌生的房間，是你的臉。牠這輩子最信任的一雙眼睛就在旁邊，牠一點都不怕。你給牠的不是慌亂，是安心。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給反覆回放毛孩臨終畫面、卡在罪惡感裡的人；讀完能鬆一口氣
variations: 牠不知道那是最後一次，牠只知道你在。對牠來說，有你在的地方，就沒有可怕的事。

en.content: You keep replaying that final moment, turning it over, wondering if you got something wrong. But here's the thing — at the very end, they weren't looking at the machines or the strange room. They were looking at your face. The eyes they trusted most in the whole world were right there, and they weren't afraid at all. What you gave them wasn't panic. It was peace.
en.editorNote: For people stuck replaying their pet's last moments in guilt; meant to let them finally exhale
variations: They didn't know it was the last time. They only knew you were there. And anywhere you were, nothing was ever scary.

items.sourceNote: 人寵壽命不對等的愧疚與感激 frame，原創（一個章節 vs 一輩子）

zh-tw.content: 我會活幾十年，你只陪了其中一小段。可是對你來說，我就是你的一輩子——從睜開眼到閉上眼，全部都是我。我常覺得虧欠你，只給了你我人生的一個章節；後來才懂，是你把那個章節，變成我這輩子最想重看的一段。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合長文貼文或紀念冊的收尾，寫毛孩與人壽命不對等那種又愧疚又感激的心情
variations: 你不是我生命的全部，但你在的那幾年，把我最好的樣子都調了出來。這樣就夠了，真的夠了。

en.content: I'll live for decades; you were only here for a small stretch of it. But to you, I was your whole life — from the day you opened your eyes to the day you closed them, all of it was me. I used to feel I'd short-changed you, giving you just one chapter of my life. Then I understood: you turned that chapter into the one I'd most want to read again.
en.editorNote: A closing line for a long post or memorial book, about the ache and gratitude of loving something with a shorter lifespan
variations: You weren't my whole life, but in the years you were here, you pulled out the best version of me. That's enough. It really is enough.

items.sourceNote: 把喪寵經驗轉成對生命/道別的體悟 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 陪你走完最後那段路，是我第一次那麼近地看著一個生命離開。我以為我會被嚇壞，結果你走得那麼安靜、那麼信任。你好像順便教了我一件事：原來道別不一定是可怕的，它也可以很溫柔。以後換我要走的那天，我大概會沒那麼怕了——因為你先示範過一次給我看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 較深、較沉澱的一則，適合忌日或事隔一段時間後的回顧書寫；把失去轉成對生命的體悟
variations: 你教會我最後一課，不是怎麼失去，是怎麼好好放手。謝謝你連要走的時候，都還在教我。

en.content: Being with you to the very end was the first time I watched a life leave from so close. I thought it would terrify me. Instead you went so quietly, so trusting. It's like you taught me one last thing on your way out: goodbyes don't have to be frightening — they can be gentle too. When it's my turn someday, I think I'll be a little less afraid — because you showed me how first.
en.editorNote: A deeper, more settled entry — good for a death anniversary or a reflection written some time later; turns the loss into a lesson about life
variations: The last thing you taught me wasn't how to lose something. It was how to let go with grace. Thank you for teaching me even as you were leaving.

items.sourceNote: grief has no timeline + 幾個月後被舊物突襲 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 都過了半年了，我以為自己好了。結果昨天大掃除，在沙發縫裡摳出一小撮你的毛，我就整個人蹲在地上哭到不行。原來想念不會按進度走，它會躲在你以為早就清乾淨的角落，等你哪天不設防，突然撲上來抱住你。沒關係，被抱到就抱回去，那也是你還在的證據。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合事隔數月、突然被舊物觸發情緒時的自我安慰貼文；點出「悲傷沒有進度表」這件事
variations: 掃到你的毛、翻到你咬爛的玩具、聞到那款肉泥的味道——這些埋伏我永遠躲不掉。但我後來不躲了，我把毛收進小盒子裡，跟它說：謝謝你還記得回來找我。

en.content: It's been six months. I thought I was okay. Then yesterday I was cleaning and dug a little tuft of your fur out of the couch cushions, and I just crumpled onto the floor. Turns out grief doesn't follow a schedule — it hides in the corners you thought you'd already cleared, and on a day your guard is down, it jumps out and wraps around you. That's okay. When it holds you, hold it back. That's proof you're still here.
en.editorNote: For the ambush of grief months later, triggered by an old object; names the truth that grief has no timeline
variations: Finding your fur, your chewed-up toy, that one treat smell — I'll never fully dodge these ambushes. So I stopped dodging. I tucked the fur into a little box and said: thank you for finding your way back to me.

items.sourceNote: disenfranchised grief / 小動物的悲傷被輕視 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 「不過是隻倉鼠而已」「一隻兔子有什麼好哭的」——如果你正因為這種話，逼自己把眼淚吞回去，我想跟你說：牠的體型很小，但牠在你生活裡佔的位置一點都不小。每天換水、剪指甲、半夜爬起來看牠有沒有在動，那些操心是真的，那份感情就是真的。悲傷不看物種，只看你們之間有多深。你難過，是應該的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 專門寫給失去兔子、鼠類、鳥、爬蟲等「非貓狗」毛孩、悲傷卻被旁人輕視的人；肯定他們的感受
variations: 沒有人會問「你養的是大狗還是小鼠」再決定要不要難過。牠陪過你、你操心過牠，這樣就夠格讓你好好哭一場。別為了讓別人自在，先把自己的痛打折。

en.content: "It was just a hamster." "You're crying over a rabbit?" If you're swallowing your tears because of lines like these, here's what I want you to know: the body was small, but the space it took up in your life was not. The daily water changes, the nail trims, getting up at 2am just to check it was still moving — that worry was real, so that love is real. Grief doesn't check the species; it checks how deep the bond ran. You're allowed to fall apart over this.
en.editorNote: Written for people grieving a rabbit, rodent, bird, or reptile whose loss others minimize; validates disenfranchised grief
variations: Nobody asks the size of the animal before deciding whether your heartbreak counts. It kept you company, you worried over it — that's enough to earn a proper cry. Don't discount your own pain just to keep other people comfortable.

items.sourceNote: 毛孩是你一整段人生的沉默見證者 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 你陪我走過的，不是幾年，是我整段最亂的日子。搬了三次家、換了兩份工作、談了幾場沒結果的戀愛，房間裡唯一沒變的，就是你。我崩潰的時候你在，我半夜回訊息笑出來的時候你也在——你是那個什麼都看在眼裡、卻從不評論一句的室友。現在那段日子過去了，你也走了。謝謝你當我那整個時代，唯一的目擊者。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合陪伴很多年、見證過主人一整段青春／低潮的毛孩；把牠寫成「人生某個時代的見證者」
variations: 別人記得的是那幾年的我，你記得的是那個沒人看見、深夜關起門的我。這世界上最懂那段日子的，其實是一隻不會說話的你。

en.content: What you were there for wasn't just a few years — it was my messiest whole era. Three moves, two jobs, a couple of relationships that went nowhere, and the one constant in every room was you. You were there when I fell apart, and there when I laughed at a text at 2am — the roommate who saw everything and never once commented. Now that chapter's over, and so are you. Thank you for being the only witness to that entire era of me.
en.editorNote: For a pet that lived through a long, formative stretch of the owner's life; frames the pet as the silent witness to an era
variations: Other people remember the version of me from those years. You remember the me behind the closed door at midnight, the one nobody saw. The one who understood that era best turned out to be a creature who couldn't say a word.

items.sourceNote: 領養紀念日／到家日 frame，把忌日以外的紀念日轉成溫柔儀式，原創

zh-tw.content: 今天是你來我家的第八年。以前這天我們會加一顆蛋、拍一張醜醜的合照。今年沒有你了，我還是煮了那顆蛋，只是自己吃掉。我沒有難過一整天，我反而想謝謝那個八年前簽下領養單、緊張得手在抖的自己——謝謝你多按了那一下確認鍵，換來我這輩子最好的八年。到家日快樂，臭寶。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合領養紀念日／到家日（不是忌日）的紀念貼文；把日子過成溫柔的慶祝而非哀悼
variations: 與其記得你走的那天，我更想記得你來的那天。那天你什麼都不知道，就這樣被我抱回家——結果從此改寫了我整個人生。到家日快樂。

en.content: Today marks eight years since you came home to me. We used to add an egg to your bowl and take one ugly photo together. This year there's no you, so I cooked the egg anyway and ate it myself. I didn't spend the day sad — instead I wanted to thank the me from eight years ago, hands shaking as I signed the adoption papers. Thank you for hitting that confirm button. It bought me the best eight years of my life. Happy gotcha day, you little menace.
en.editorNote: For an adoption / gotcha-day anniversary (not the death anniversary); turns the date into a gentle celebration rather than mourning
variations: Instead of remembering the day you left, I'd rather remember the day you arrived. You had no idea what was happening — you just got scooped up and carried home, and then you went and rewrote my entire life. Happy gotcha day.

items.sourceNote: 極短句，適合刺青／刻字／小卡的告別語 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 同一個世界，換一個位置等我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 極短句，適合刺青、項圈吊牌刻字、紀念小卡或社群大頭貼下方的一句話；留白給讀者想像
variations: 先去玩，晚點見。
牽過的那條線，一直都還在。

en.content: Same world. Just waiting for me in a different spot.
en.editorNote: A very short line for a tattoo, an engraved tag, a memorial card, or a caption under a profile photo; leaves room for the reader to fill in
variations: Go play. See you soon.
The leash between us never actually dropped.

items.sourceNote: 手機相簿捨不得刪 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 手機裡還留著三千多張你的照片，一張都刪不掉。不是捨不得空間，是捨不得那個滑過去、還像你在的錯覺。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些不敢打開相簿、卻也刪不掉照片的飼主；適合貼在社群或私訊安慰同樣心情的人
variations: 相簿我不敢點開，可是更不敢刪。就讓它一直滿著吧，滿得像你從來沒走。

en.content: There are still three thousand photos of you on my phone, and I can't delete a single one. It's not the storage — it's that scrolling past them still feels, for half a second, like you're here.
en.editorNote: For someone who can't open the album but can't clear it either; works as a caption or a private message to someone in the same place
variations: I won't open the album, but I won't delete it either. Let it stay full — full like you never left.

items.sourceNote: 「只有遺忘才是真正的離開」＋衣物裡的毛 frame，原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 換季整理衣服，一根你的毛從袖口飄出來。我先笑了一下，才紅了眼——原來你還藏在我每一件外套裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給離世一段時間後、仍不時在生活角落遇見毛孩痕跡的人；把這些提醒理解成溫柔的同行，而不是折磨
variations: 地板掃了好幾次，還是會冒出一根你的毛。我不再急著清掉了，那是你偷偷留給我的訊息。

en.content: Changing out my closet, one of your hairs drifted out of a sleeve. I smiled before my eyes went hot — turns out you're still tucked into every coat I own.
en.editorNote: For someone who keeps meeting traces of their pet in daily corners long after; reframes the reminders as gentle company rather than torment
variations: I've swept the floor a dozen times and still one of your hairs turns up. I've stopped rushing to clear it away — it's a message you left me.

items.sourceNote: 身體慣性仍在運作的失落 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 早上四點還是自己醒了，手往床邊一伸，才想起那裡已經空了。原來身體比心先記得，你已經不用我餵了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合描述離世初期「身體還在照舊運作」的失落；讓有同樣經驗的人知道自己並不奇怪
variations: 買飼料時，手還是先伸向你那一牌，結帳前才回過神——架上那包，再也沒有人等著吃了。

en.content: I still woke on my own at four in the morning, reached for the side of the bed, and only then remembered it was empty. My body remembered before my heart did — you don't need me to feed you anymore.
en.editorNote: For the early days when the body's old habits keep running on their own; reassures people with the same experience that they aren't strange
variations: My hand still reaches for your brand of food at the store. I only catch myself at the register — that bag on the shelf has no one waiting to eat it now.

items.sourceNote: 季節轉冷、想念體溫 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 今年冬天特別冷。不是天氣的問題，是腳邊少了那一團會自己發熱的小暖爐。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合天氣轉冷、特別想念毛孩體溫的時刻；短而有畫面，適合社群貼文配一張舊照
variations: 以前老嫌你把整張床都占滿，現在床都是我的了，我卻只想把位置全還給你。

en.content: Winter feels colder this year. It's not the weather — it's the little furnace that used to warm itself against my feet, gone.
en.editorNote: For when the season turns and you miss their body heat most; short and vivid, pairs well with an old photo on social
variations: I used to complain you took up the whole bed. Now the whole bed is mine, and all I want is to give your spot back.

items.sourceNote: 多寵家庭、另一隻毛孩也在找 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 家裡那隻還在你常睡的角落聞了又聞，然後回頭看我。我不知道怎麼跟牠解釋，只好抱著牠，一起等一個不會再回來的腳步聲。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合多寵家庭；寫出另一隻毛孩也在找、也在難過的畫面，陪伴同樣正在失落的家人
variations: 牠開始睡到你以前的位置了。我沒有阻止——也許牠是想替你，把我好好顧著。

en.content: The one still here keeps sniffing the corner where you used to sleep, then turns to look at me. I don't know how to explain it, so I just hold them, and we wait together for footsteps that aren't coming back.
en.editorNote: For multi-pet homes; captures the surviving pet searching and grieving too, and holding a family that has also lost someone
variations: They've started sleeping in your old spot. I didn't stop them — maybe they're trying to look after me in your place.

items.sourceNote: 「房子變成另一個形狀」— 搬離毛孩住過的家 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 搬家那天，最後一趟我回去拿垃圾袋。空屋子裡，我蹲下來摸了摸門框上那排抓痕——你以前每次聽到我鑰匙聲就會這樣扒。房東說會補土重漆。我沒有反對，只是站在那裡，把那面牆多看了三十秒。有些東西帶不走，只能記得。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合搬離毛孩住過的家、要跟那個空間告別的時刻；寫給覺得「連牠留下的痕跡都保不住」的人
variations: 新家很好，採光比舊家好太多。可是我一直在找一個位置——那個以前你會趴著曬太陽的位置。原來我搬的不是家具，是一個沒有你的格局。

en.content: Moving day. I went back one last time for the trash bags. Standing in the empty place, I crouched down and ran my thumb over the claw marks on the door frame — you did that every time you heard my keys. The landlord says he'll fill them in and repaint. I didn't argue. I just stood there and looked at that wall for thirty more seconds. Some things you can't pack. You can only remember them.
en.editorNote: For leaving the home your pet lived in; written for people who feel like they can't even keep the marks their pet left behind
variations: The new place is good — better light than the old one. But I keep hunting for a spot: the patch of floor where you used to lie in the sun. Turns out I wasn't moving furniture. I was moving into a floor plan with no you in it.

items.sourceNote: 打雷／颱風夜，過去負責安撫牠的人突然無事可做 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 昨天半夜打雷，我整個人彈起來坐直，第一個念頭是——你在哪裡，你會怕。然後才想起來，今年不用再把你從桌子底下挖出來、抱著你數秒數等雷停了。窗外雨很大，屋子裡很安靜。安靜到我居然有點希望，你還在這裡怕一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合颱風夜、打雷、放煙火的夜晚；那些以前要負責安撫牠、現在突然沒事可做的時刻
variations: 以前每逢過年鞭炮聲，我會把電視音量開大、抱著你坐在最裡面那間房。今年鞭炮照放，我一個人坐在客廳，才發現那些年怕的人不只是你。

en.content: Thunder cracked in the middle of last night and I sat straight up — first thought, where are you, you're going to be scared. Then I remembered I don't have to coax you out from under the table anymore, don't have to hold you and count seconds until it passes. Heavy rain outside, dead quiet inside. Quiet enough that some part of me wished you were still here being afraid.
en.editorNote: For storm nights, thunder, and fireworks — the moments you used to be in charge of calming them, and now have nothing to do
variations: Every New Year I'd turn the TV up and sit with you in the back room while the firecrackers went off. They went off again this year. I sat in the living room alone and realized you were never the only one who was scared.

items.sourceNote: 離世後遇到人生好事、最想報喜的那一個不在了 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 今天收到那封錄取信，我尖叫完、打給我媽、傳給朋友，然後拿著手機在客廳站了三秒——才想起來，我還漏了一個人。你以前根本聽不懂我在講什麼，你只知道我聲音變高了就跟著轉圈。我最後還是把好消息說出口了，對著空空的沙發，聲音有點抖。你聽到了對不對。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合毛孩離世後遇到人生好事、卻發現「最想分享的那一個不在了」的時刻；也適合放在畢業、換工作、結婚的紀念貼文
variations: 結婚那天，親友都到齊了，只有你缺席。我在口袋裡放了一張你的照片，敬酒的時候摸了一下——這樣就算你有來過。

en.content: The offer letter came today. I screamed, called my mom, texted my friends, then stood in the living room holding my phone for three seconds before I realized I'd skipped someone. You never understood a word of it anyway — you just knew my voice went high, and that meant it was time to spin in circles. I said it out loud anyway, to an empty couch, and my voice shook a little. You heard me, right?
en.editorNote: For good news that lands after they're gone, when the one you most want to tell isn't there; also works for graduation, new job, or wedding posts
variations: Everyone I love showed up to the wedding except you. I kept a photo of you in my pocket and touched it during the toast. Close enough to you being there.

items.sourceNote: 長輩失去毛孩、整日作息崩塌，晚輩該怎麼陪 frame，原創

zh-tw.content: 如果家裡的長輩剛送走毛孩，請多留意他。對一個退休的人來說，那隻狗不只是一隻狗，是他一整天的行程表——早上六點要出門、中午要餵藥、晚上要繞公園兩圈。現在整張表空白了。別急著說「不要想那麼多」，你可以說：「爸，明天早上那圈我陪你走。」把空掉的那幾個小時，先用陪伴補起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合家中長輩失去毛孩時；提醒晚輩「作息垮掉」往往比悲傷本身更難撐，並提供一句具體可執行的邀請
variations: 不要自作主張幫他把碗跟牽繩收起來，那是他的節奏，不是你的。等他哪天自己願意收了，你再幫忙拿去洗就好。

en.content: If an older person in your family just lost a pet, keep an eye on them. For someone retired, that dog wasn't just a dog — it was the whole day's schedule.
